key_insight: An interpretable inverse framework recovers relative spatial variations in multiple hyperelastic constitutive parameters from displacement fields alone.
engineering_relevance: Mapping heterogeneous material properties could support functionally graded materials, composite design, and biological tissue characterization.
method: Use full-field displacements to identify spatially varying constitutive parameters.
Exploit the inverse problem’s linear structure and optimize parameters directly at the finite-element level.
evidence_signal: Validation on 3D synthetic and 2D experimental benchmarks spanning heterogeneous, graded, and anisotropic hyperelastic materials showed acceptable accuracy with substantially lower computation time than recently reported deep-learning frameworks.
watch_item: The framework identifies relative parameter variations; absolute calibration and robustness to noisy experimental displacements require scrutiny.
paper_title: Interpretable identification of constitutive parameter field for three-dimensional heterogeneous and graded hyperelastic materials from full-field displacements
